items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(b) covers readings in both affected rooms. The estimate allows €90 for a distinct measurement charge; §7.1.8(c) bars charging again for the same work under line 4.
Section 7.1.7(b) covers drying mats on the wet strip of oak boards. The single flat rate follows the €242 prior and is distinct from utility-room dehumidification.
Section 7.1.7(b) expressly covers drying the air volume of the affected utility room. Allow about €250 gross for the separate dehumidifier charge, not for drying unaffected parts of the hall.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers the documented four technician-hours at about €61.50 per hour, or €246 gross. Section 7.1.8(c) excludes any overlap with work already charged on lines 1–3.
Section 7.1.7(h) covers removing the detergent and lint film from the wetted tiles and oak. Allow €110 gross for one targeted clean, not general housekeeping.

Section 7.1.7(e) covers identifying the source and confirming that the washer and connections no longer leak, even if the appliance itself is uninsured. Allow €144 gross for the inspection and test, consistent with the prior.

items.description: Remove and dispose of damaged skirting
items.rationale: Sections 7.1.7(a) and 5.2.1 cover removal and disposal of the damaged trim. The 4.5 m in the utility room plus 5.5 m along both sides of the wet hall stretch supports all 10 m and the €768 gross prior.
Fixed skirting is insured under §4.2.2, and §§7.1.5 and 7.1.9 limit replacement to the damaged runs at the original profile and finish. All 10 m are supported, so the gross prior of €1,348 applies.

Section 5.2.6 includes specialist transport but gives restoration first call on the shared €1,190 gross cap, leaving no expected balance. The €120 estimate is conditional on a balance being available.
Section 5.2.6 requires a specialist assessment but pays it only from the balance left after restoration and earlier invoiced transport. No balance is expected; €180 is the conditional gross estimate.

Section 5.2.6 covers conservation drying and stabilisation, but restoration is expected to exhaust the shared cap before this line is reached. The €300 estimate is conditional on sufficient cap remaining.

The painting is not individually recorded in the schedule, so §5.2.6 caps all conservation costs at €1,000 plus 19% VAT actually incurred under §7.7. Restoration takes priority and is expected to absorb the full €1,190 gross.
